about: Domaine Saint-Préfert was founded in the 1920s by Fernand Serre, an Avignon pharmacist and wine lover, in the south of the Châteauneuf-du-Pape appellation. In 2002 Isabel Ferrando, a former banker who had trained in Gigondas, bought the estate from the Serre family and made her first vintage in 2003. In two decades she has become one of the appellation’s most admired growers; her daughter Guillemette now works alongside her. With the 2021 vintage the estate’s reds were reorganised under a single name, “Famille Isabel Ferrando.”

This red comes from the Les Serres parcel, from fruit that once went into the domaine’s Auguste Favier and Charles Giraud cuvées, on rolled pebbles, blue clay, gravel and sand. The blend is 75% old-vine Grenache with Cinsault, Mourvèdre and a touch of Syrah. The vineyards are organic and biodynamic, the grapes hand-picked and fermented as whole clusters with native yeasts, then aged about 18 months, mostly in demi-muids, with some amphora.

Critics have praised the 2021 for its finesse in a cooler, fresher vintage: Jeb Dunnuck rated it 95 points, and La Revue du Vin de France gave it 93. Farr Vintners suggests drinking it from 2024 to 2034. In the glass it shows black raspberry, Provençal herbs and ground pepper, with fine-grained tannins and an elegant, focused finish.
